title: Entry fee versus per-visit fee
hook: A fixed access fee and a smaller visit charge cross a pay-per-visit total.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate a fixed-access versus per-visit crossover.

misconception: A smaller per-visit charge guarantees a smaller total.
objective: Calculate a fixed-access versus per-visit crossover.

claims.text: Fictional A charges €10 per visit. B charges €30 once plus €4 per visit; service is assumed equivalent. Scaled model; fictional prices; equivalent service; no recommendation.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Visits=3, A=€30 and B=€42. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",10,"x"]; B=["+",30,["*",4,"x"]]; x denotes Visits. At x=3, A=30, B=42; recall at x=6: B=54. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Separate the one-time term from the per-visit term. The two totals match at five visits in this model. The comparison does not determine which service fits someone’s needs or predict future attendance.

recall.question: Fictional A charges €10 per visit. B charges €30 once plus €4 per visit; service is assumed equivalent. Change only Visits to 6. What is B (Fee+visits) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Visits=6: it gives €54. Separate the one-time term from the per-visit term. The two totals match at five visits in this model. The comparison does not determine which service fits someone’s needs or predict future attendance.
